newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan takes "difficult" decisions to get IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan takes "difficult" decisions to get IMF loan.

text.p: The Pakistani cabinet decided on Thursday to take "bold and difficult" decisions to meet current economic problems and meet IMF conditions for the release of a stalled standby loan, a government statement said.
It said a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto approved a framework to conclude an arrangement with the International Monetary Fund. It gave no details.
The decision came after Pakistani markets were braced for a possible "mini-budget" aimed at persuading the IMF to release delayed tranches of a $600 million standby loan.

The government statement said the cabinet was briefed about the damage done to the economy by strikes over some two-and-a-half months in protest against the state budget for fiscal 1996-97 (July/June) which was packed with harsh taxes.

"The cabinet felt that in order to offset the negative impact of those strikes and other negative factors, bold and difficult decisions needed to be taken in the interest of consolidating a sustained economic growth and quickening the country's march towards meaningful progress," it said.
"However, the cabinet felt that even difficult decisions will have to be so taken as to make them as less painful as possible and without jeopardising in any way Pakistan's security interests."
